source.author: verg
source.text: Vix ea dicta: dehinc progressus monstrat et aram et Carmentalem Romani nomine portam quam memorant, nymphae priscum Carmentis honorem, vatis fatidicae, cecinit quae prima futuros Aeneadas magnos et nobile Pallanteum.
source.text_original: Vix ea dicta: dehinc progressus monstrat et aram / et Carmentalem Romani nomine portam / quam memorant, nymphae priscum Carmentis honorem, / vatis fatidicae, cecinit quae prima futuros / Aeneadas magnos et nobile Pallanteum.
source.text_english: Scarcely had he said these things; then, advancing, he shows both the altar and the gate which they call Carmentalis by the Roman name, the ancient honor of the nymph Carmentis, the prophetic seer, who first sang of the great descendants of Aeneas and noble Pallanteum that were to come.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_original: Prima deum magnis canimus freta pervia natis / fatidicamque ratem, Scythici quae Phasidis oras / ausa sequi mediosque inter iuga concita cursus / rumpere flammifero tandem consedit Olympo.
reuse.text_english: First we sing of the sea passages made traversable by the great sons of the gods, and of the prophetic ship, which, daring to follow the Scythian shores of Phasis and, driven on, to break through its course amid the middle mountain ridges, at last settled on fiery Olympus.
